region: Hector · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: The Hazlitt family has farmed the eastern shore of Seneca Lake since 1852, when they bought 153 acres in Hector that already had orchards and vines. Grapes grew there for more than a century before the late Jerry and Elaine Hazlitt opened a winery in 1985 in an old horse barn, which is still the tasting room. Their Red Cat became one of New York’s best-selling wines. Today sixth-generation siblings Doug Hazlitt and Leigh Hazlitt Triner lead one of the largest family-owned wineries in the Finger Lakes.

Alongside the popular wines, Hazlitt makes a serious line from its estate vinifera vineyards on Seneca Lake’s “banana belt.” A Meritage is a blend of the Bordeaux red grapes. Hazlitt’s comes from estate Cabernet Franc, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon, and the winery’s reserve Meritage is aged in French oak barrels. Seneca Lake’s depth moderates the climate along its shores, which helps these later-ripening grapes mature this far north.

The 2021 opens with caramel, vanilla and cinnamon from the barrel, then sweet cherry, with light strawberry on the finish. Reviewers also note blackberry, baking spice, subtle herbal undertones, bright acidity and soft tannins: a supple, medium-bodied Finger Lakes red. Cool-climate Meritage blends like this are leaner and fresher than their California cousins, and they are better at the table than as a showpiece. Pair it with roast pork, duck or anything off the grill.
